description: HRI-VIS is the visible CCD camera of the Deep Impact High Resolution Instrument. A dichroic sends visible light through a nine-position filter wheel; the PDS ground-calibration tables are manufacturer witness-sample transmission profiles for those positions.
short_description: Deep Impact High Resolution Instrument visible CCD filters
facility_description: Deep Impact was a NASA comet mission whose flyby spacecraft carried the High Resolution Instrument and Medium Resolution Instrument; the same flyby cameras were later used in the EPOXI extended mission.
notes: NJM names Blue_fil, Clear1_fil, Clear6_fil, Green_fil, IR_fil, NIR_fil, Orange_fil, Red_fil and Violet_fil are omitted. The SVO Filter Profile Service pages that distinguish a filter-only product did not load (curl HTTP 000 timeouts; page open failed), and no opened PDS label uses a _fil name. The opened tables are filter witness-sample transmissions, not a separate filter-plus-CCD product. The PDS label calls the instrument the High Resolution Instrument; the flight AICD also says High Resolution Imager (HRI). The AICD says the wheel has two clear apertures and 7 filters, with five filters roughly 100 nm wide centered at 450, 550, 650, 750 and 850 nm. The Earth HRIV catalog lists the same named filters and points effective centers and FWHM to Klaasen et al. (2013), whose catalog key KLAASENETAL2011 is still worded as accepted for publication and does not print a DOI; Crossref shows doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2013.03.024 for EPOXI instrument calibration. The older flight AICD still says the calibration paper was submitted to Optical Engineering; the later reference catalog prints Rev. Sci. Instrum., 79, 091301, 2008, doi:10.1063/1.2972112. No magnitude system is stated. PDS dataset pages give a citation to use for each data set; that is a citation request, not an acknowledgement paragraph, so acknowledgements is empty. ADS abstract pages returned HTTP 405 behind a human-verification challenge. The NASA licence page qualifies that sentence: it applies unless the data file is marked with a restrictive notice or license.

licence.terms: "There are no restrictions on the usage of these data."

Blue.Description: HRIV filter-wheel position 2, called blue, centered at 450 nm with a width of 100 nm.
Blue.Comments: Transmission profile in the PDS TV4 table, measured by the manufacturer on a witness sample.

Clear1.Description: HRIV filter-wheel position 1, an uncoated clear aperture.
Clear1.Comments: Witness-sample transmission is 90 percent or greater from 299 through 1200 nanometers.

Clear6.Description: HRIV filter-wheel position 6, a second uncoated clear aperture.
Clear6.Comments: Witness-sample transmission is 90 percent or greater from 299 through 1200 nanometers.

Green.Description: HRIV filter-wheel position 3, called green, centered at 550 nm with a width of 100 nm.
Green.Comments: Transmission profile in the PDS TV4 table, measured by the manufacturer on a witness sample.

IR.Description: HRIV filter-wheel position 5, a longpass filter the label calls effectively centered at 950 nm.
IR.Comments: The label says the longpass starts at 900 nm and that the CCD response defines the long-wavelength cutoff at about 960 nm.

NIR.Description: HRIV filter-wheel position 8, called near-IR, centered at 850 nm with a width of 100 nm.
NIR.Comments: Transmission profile in the PDS TV4 table, measured by the manufacturer on a witness sample.

Orange.Description: HRIV filter-wheel position 9, called orange, centered at 650 nm with a width of 100 nm.
Orange.Comments: Transmission profile in the PDS TV4 table, measured by the manufacturer on a witness sample.

Red.Description: HRIV filter-wheel position 7, called red, centered at 750 nm with a width of 100 nm.
Red.Comments: Transmission profile in the PDS TV4 table, measured by the manufacturer on a witness sample.

Violet.Description: HRIV filter-wheel position 4, called violet, centered at 350 nm with a width of 100 nm and a shortpass coating.
Violet.Comments: The label says the substrate produces a cut-on wavelength of about 340 nanometers.
